note: Adapted from Bacchus's (1997) redescription of the species (in English); the alate, soldier and major worker all have prose descriptions and measurement tables, and a lectotype and a junior synonym are designated here (Microtermes usambaricus Sjöstedt, 1926, syn. n.). The original description is Sjöstedt 1904 (Termes (Microtermes) redenianus). The first row of the soldier measurement table in the OCR (head including the mandibles) reads 'P20=38 12 22', the figures being illegible, so they are not recorded; the pronotum width row reads '1.21-1.40' and is read here as 1.21—1.40 from its proportion to the hind tibia of 1.43—1.53.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule red-orange, sometimes darker above the ocelli and behind the eyes; frons paler; the head surface with many minute yellow dots scattered at the hair bases; anteclypeus, postclypeus and labrum yellow; antennae pale yellow; pronotum pale orange; abdominal tergites and sternites slightly paler than the pronotum, legs dull yellow. Wings pale yellow, the costa darker. Posterior margin of the head capsule broad and evenly rounded; head hairs brown, with both short and long hairs above and behind the compound eyes, the longest just reaching or not reaching beyond the outer margin of the compound eyes; vertex flat in the region of the frontal gland pore; frons slightly rough with weak wrinkling; cranial suture almost invisible. Compound eyes and ocelli oval; postclypeus arcuate with a shallow reticulation and a faint to distinct longitudinal median suture; labrum wider than long; antennae 16-segmented, segments 3, 4 and 5 about the same size, segments 1 and 2 about equal. Pronotum hairy, the anterior and posterior margins slightly concave; posterior margin of the meso- and metanota deeply incurved, without a median longitudinal line.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule and labrum yellow to orange; mandibles brown with a yellow base; antennae pale yellow to yellow; postmentum concolorous with the cheeks; nota, body and legs pale yellow to yellow. Head capsule short-oval and almost circular, the posterior margin broadly rounded; short hairs numerous on the sides, long hairs few; labrum tongue-shaped, about as long as wide, extending over 0.65 of the total mandible length; dorsum with many hairs, 8—10 hairs in the anterior third; mandibles moderately stout, the tip moderately incurved, the degree of curvature 0.04—0.06 mm. Antennae 14-segmented, segments 3 and 4 similar, segments 1 and 2 about equal; postmentum short and wide. Pronotum saddle-shaped, with short hairs and several long ones; anterior margin with a deep V-shaped median notch, posterior margin nearly straight. Fore tibia moderately to strongly swollen; spurs 3, the dorsal spur short, about half the length of the outer ventral spur; the long hair on the fore coxa not spine-like.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Major worker: head capsule yellow, body, legs and antennae pale yellow; postclypeal pad dull yellowish brown; mandibles brown with a yellow base. Head capsule almost square to almost rectangular, the sides parallel.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Alate measurements (4 specimens, 2 colonies, mm): head length to the anterior margin of the postclypeus 1.18—1.25, head width including the compound eyes 1.33—1.43, postclypeus length 0.30—0.33 and width 0.56—0.63, labrum length 0.35—0.43 and width 0.50, greatest compound eye diameter 0.36—0.43 and least diameter 0.34—0.38, greatest ocellus diameter 0.20—0.23 and least diameter 0.15, ocellus-to-compound-eye distance 0.05—0.08, pronotum length 0.83—0.95 and width 1.21—1.40, hind tibia length 1.43—1.53. Soldier measurements (22 specimens, 19 colonies): head length to the base of the mandibles 0.73—0.88, head width behind the antennal fossae 0.60—0.75, greatest head width 0.69—0.80, labrum length 0.26—0.33 and width 0.22—0.28, left mandible transverse length 0.50—0.55, width 0.04—0.05, curvature 0.04—0.06, fore tibia length 0.55—0.63 and width 0.15—0.18, hind tibia length 0.63—0.70 and width 0.10—0.13, greatest pronotum width 0.48—0.57, postmentum length 0.40—0.45, greatest width 0.33—0.38. Soldier lectotype (Tanzania, AMNH, designated here); the lectotype soldier of the synonym Microtermes usambaricus Sjöstedt, 1926 (Tanzania, NR) is also designated here, as a new synonym.
